data.title: Annovis Bio: Buy Rating Reiterated as Buntanetap Nears Key Alzheimer’s Phase 3 and CTAD Milestones; Price Target Maintained at $8
data.description:

Jason McCarthy has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors related to Annovis Bio’s lead asset, buntanetap, and the advancing Alzheimer’s program. The company has fully enrolled its pivotal Phase 3 trial in early Alzheimer’s disease with a strong biomarker-positive patient population, and is approaching database lock and a six‑month top‑line readout that could support an NDA submission shortly thereafter.

In addition, multiple oral and poster presentations at the CTAD conference will showcase buntanetap’s differentiated mechanism of action, the rigor of the Phase 3 trial design, and Annovis’s application of AI for blood‑brain barrier prediction and regulatory preparation, underscoring innovation and execution. Taken together, these clinical, regulatory, and technology milestones underpin McCarthy’s confidence in value creation potential, leading him to reiterate a Buy rating with an unchanged $8 price target.

Jason McCarthy’s rating is based on Annovis Bio’s progress in advancing buntanetap through late‑stage development. The company exceeded its original enrollment target in the pivotal early Alzheimer’s study, suggesting strong patient and investigator engagement, and is on track for database lock in 4Q26 and top‑line data in 1Q27, which, if positive, would support an NDA submission in 2Q27.

data.title: Jefferies Maintains Hold on Bloom Energy as Strong Near-Term Momentum Is Offset by Strategic Risks and a Trimmed Price Target from $264 to $242
data.description:
Julien Dumoulin Smith, an analyst from Jefferies, maintained the Hold rating on Bloom Energy. The associated price target was lowered to $242.00.

Julien Dumoulin Smith has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors that balance strong near-term performance with lingering strategic uncertainties. Bloom Energy delivered a standout quarter and again raised its 2026 revenue and margin outlook, supported by accelerating demand, capacity expansion plans beyond 5 GW, and a growing ability to deploy power quickly, but investors still lack clarity on backlog details and the trajectory of key projects like ORCL’s Project Jupiter.

Customer concentration, while modestly improving, remains elevated, and newly disclosed multi-year supply commitments materially heighten working capital and execution risk if deployments are delayed. At the same time, visibility beyond the mid‑to‑late 2020s is limited, and the valuation already embeds much of the expected growth, leading Jefferies to trim its price target from $264 to $242 as sector multiples compress. Taken together, these factors support a neutral stance: the operational momentum is clear, but the risk profile and limited long-term transparency justify maintaining a Hold rating rather than moving to a more bullish recommendation.

data.title: SCYNEXIS Buy Rating Reaffirmed as Advancing Antifungal Pipeline and BARDA Support Underpin Unchanged $32 Price Target
data.description:
In a report released yesterday, Jason McCarthy from Maxim Group maintained a Buy rating on SCYNEXIS, with a price target of $32.00.

Jason McCarthy has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors tied to SCYNEXIS’s advancing antifungal pipeline and de-risked clinical profile. He views the positive Phase 1 data for SCY-247’s IV formulation as a pivotal milestone, since it enables both IV and oral versions to move into Phase 2 for invasive candidiasis with target drug exposures already achieved and a clean tolerability profile. The ability to offer both IV and oral formulations, including oral step-down therapy, is seen as a competitive advantage in a field with few effective options and rising resistance to existing azole antifungals.

McCarthy also emphasizes that SCYNEXIS is developing SCY-247 in a novel triterpenoid class with broad, fungicidal activity, building on the company’s track record from ibrexafungerp, which was licensed to GSK and has late-stage data in serious fungal infections. His conviction is strengthened by the BARDA contract of up to roughly $214 million, which materially supports SCY-247’s development and validates the strategic importance of the program. He further notes the company’s solid cash position and additional pipeline asset SCY-770 in ADPKD as incremental drivers, leading him to maintain an unchanged price target of $32 and a Buy rating on the stock.
